_readme: STANDING AUTHORITY for the autonomous build loop. Project-local, gitignored,
per-machine: a fresh machine needs it written again, and the loop's handoff
says so.
THE RULE THAT KEEPS THIS SAFE: every entry names a SCRIPT or a bounded CLI
verb the loop is ORDERED to run by its own prompt. No entry names a shell, a
container exec, a raw database client, or a history-rewriting git command:
those are grants to do anything, which is what the permission classifier
exists to refuse.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT, and stays absent:
deploys, pushes and publishes: a person confirms every one
git reset/--force: history is not the loop's to rewrite
.env, secrets, this file: the loop may not widen its own authority
.claude/test-freeze.json: the loop may not unfreeze its own tests
bare docker/psql/sh: unbounded
AN ALLOWLISTED SCRIPT IS ONLY AS BOUNDED AS THE LOOP'S ABILITY TO EDIT IT:
lane-cut and pre-barrier source scripts/lane-cut.conf, and the loop edits
scripts. Review diffs to scripts/ and package.json at each record. That
includes scripts/checks/: guards.py runs every check script the ledger names.
IF A COMMAND IS REFUSED ANYWAY: the loop tries ONCE, records the refusal
verbatim in the barrier artefact, puts the exact command on the person's
list, and proceeds degraded. It never splits the command up, never routes it
through another tool, and never asks a peer session to run it: a peer
running a denied command launders the user's decision.
